clue.text: Disclose bonus represented by high honour

indicators.note: bonus is represented in a new form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a high British honour

explanation.surface: Someone reveals that their bonus came in the form of a lofty award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' looks like part of the honours story, but it is the rearranging signal; OM, the Order of Merit, is a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: To unburden one's feelings is to reveal them, a literary synonym for confess or disclose.

clue.text: Biased as a Parisian? Exactly

parts.note: un is French for a
just means exactly

explanation.surface: Is a Frenchman prejudiced? Precisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair and partial, the opposite of even-handed.

clue.text: Feast which, in France, reaches from bar to table-top

parts.note: to ban is to bar
que is French for which
the top letter of table

explanation.surface: A French feast that stretches the whole length from the bar to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reaches from ... to' just strings the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: A large formal meal is a feast.

clue.text: Cruel don's disposition to be a villain

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written, its S included

explanation.surface: A harsh academic's temperament marks him as a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but means arrangement: rearrange CRUEL DONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or rascal is a villain.

clue.text: Parsimonious attitude causing rows among well-borers

indicators.note: among puts the rows within the word for the boring tools

parts.note: a miser is a large auger used for boring wells
lines are rows

explanation.surface: A stingy outlook that leads to quarrels among well-diggers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' looks like quarrels but means lines; a miser is also a well-boring auger.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinginess, hoarding money, is a parsimonious outlook.

clue.text: Language of Hood's murderer repelling US Intelligence

parts.note: Eugene Aram, the murderer in Thomas Hood's poem The Dream of Eugene Aram

indicators.note: repelling pushes the agency's letters back, so they are read in reverse order

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: A tale of a killer from a poem fending off American spies.
explanation.walkthrough: Hood is the poet Thomas Hood, not Robin Hood; 'repelling' is the backwards signal for the agency's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Semitic tongue, spoken by Jesus, is a language of the Near East.

clue.text: A point made twice by Balaam's reproacher

indicators.note: made twice means the point letter appears two times

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A remark repeated by the creature that rebuked a prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Numbers 22, Balaam's donkey speaks to rebuke him.

clue.text: Beautiful woman in blue film

definitions.meaning: the word in the title of the 1930 film The Blue ...

explanation.surface: A lovely actress appearing in an adult movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A lovely woman may be called a heavenly being, and that word completes the title of Marlene Dietrich's film The Blue Angel.

clue.text: It shows the tides for a waterway rising about a metre

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the waterway goes round the metre
rising in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a canal is a waterway

explanation.surface: A tide table for a waterway that has risen about a metre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M inside CANAL (CANAML); 'rising' turns that to LMANAC after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual reference book of calendars that lists tide times, sunrises and the like.

clue.text: Being despised makes prisoner act like the devil

parts.note: a con is a convict
the devil tempts people to sin

explanation.surface: Being looked down on turns a convict into a devilish tempter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held in disdain, as in fall into scorn, is the state of being despised.

clue.text: Patriots hiding gin concoction among the beams

indicators.note: among puts the mixed-up drink inside the word for beams

parts.note: joists are the beams supporting a floor

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed

explanation.surface: Patriots stashing a homemade gin up in the rafters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' is the mixing signal on gin and 'among' the insertion signal; 'hiding' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Jingoism is aggressive patriotism, so its devotees are flag-waving nationalists.

clue.text: Street urchin in drink before midday

indicators.note: in places the morning abbreviation inside the word for the drink

parts.note: gin is a drink
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A street kid drinking before lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived word for a ragged child who lives on the streets.

clue.text: Disdainfully reject new stimulus at first

parts.note: a spur is a stimulus or incentive

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word new

explanation.surface: Someone scornfully turns down a fresh incentive.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff or scorn something is to reject it with contempt.

clue.text: Strong suggestion of party man taken in about church

indicators.note: taken in means held within, so the party man sits inside the other two pieces

parts.note: re means about, concerning
CE is the Church of England
a do is a party
Len is a man's name

explanation.surface: A hint that a politician was swallowed up by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party man' suggests a politician but splits into a party and a man's name; 'taken in' means enclosed by the two outer pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A word meaning a scent, used figuratively for something that evokes or hints at another thing.

clue.text: Intend to support fight, say, with two functions

indicators.note: to support in a down clue places the intend word beneath the fight word
say means the fight word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a duel is a fight
to purpose is to intend

explanation.surface: Planning to back a battle, so to speak, that serves two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving two uses or roles at once.

clue.text: A top man's cure, it turned out, for undue fuss

indicators.note: turned out means made into something different, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, the S counting as a letter

explanation.surface: A senior figure's remedy, as it happened, for making a mountain out of a molehill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turned out' rearranges A TOP MAN'S CURE IT, fourteen letters with the S of man's included.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a great commotion over a trivial matter.

clue.text: A sine qua non in identifying this oil

definitions.meaning: a volatile plant extract used in perfumery is named with this word

explanation.surface: Something indispensable in recognising a certain oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Indispensable is the first sense; a concentrated plant extract, as in lavender oil, takes the same word.

clue.text: Champion counsel

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to back or speak up for
a barrister or lawyer who pleads in court

explanation.surface: A top-class legal adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a cause is one sense; a pleader in court, as in Scotland's bar, is the other.

clue.text: Photographer's technique for revealing a look-alike's misdeeds?

definitions.meaning: superimposing two images on one frame of film
uncovering the wrongs of someone's twin, read humorously

explanation.surface: A camera trick that also unmasks the crimes of someone's double.
explanation.definitionFit: Two shots on one negative is the camera trick; a double's wrongdoing laid bare is the jokey second reading.

clue.text: Raise status of riding class

parts.note: up means riding, as a jockey is up on a horse
a grade is a class

explanation.surface: Promoting a horse-riding lesson to a higher level.
explanation.walkthrough: A jockey on a horse is said to be up.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote or improve something's rank.

clue.text: They top galleys without hesitation — houses too

annotationWithheld.why: They top galleys without hesitation — houses too (7): ROOFERS reads as ROOFS housing ER, but galleys (PROOFS) gives ROOFS only by dropping a P no clue word names, and no other parse fits
annotationWithheld.clue: They top galleys without hesitation — houses too

clue.text: Filaments beginning to burn in flames

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for flames

parts.note: fires are flames

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of burn

explanation.surface: Threads catching fire as the flames take hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives B; 'in' puts it into FIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Threads or strands are fine filaments.

clue.text: Could be a singer or one making the arrangements

indicators.note: could be signals the letters may be turned into another word

explanation.surface: A vocalist, or perhaps the event planner.
explanation.definitionFit: A planner or coordinator is a person who arranges things.

clue.text: Parade with knights outside a Scottish town

indicators.note: outside puts the knights round the parade word

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight, twice for plural
to air is to parade or show off

explanation.surface: A procession with mounted knights in a Highland town.
explanation.walkthrough: NAIRN is a town near Inverness in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town on the Moray Firth in Scotland.

clue.text: One complaint about Ruth's mother-in-law

indicators.note: about turns the whole phrase round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a moan is a complaint

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a biblical in-law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns I + MOAN round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth, Ruth stays loyal to her husband's mother, the widow from Bethlehem.

clue.text: Fine instrument, but a scholar rejected it

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word it is turned round

explanation.surface: A lovely violin, but an academic turned it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is the backwards signal; MA for a scholar is a standard convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cremonese Amati family made prized violins, so the name stands for one of their instruments.

clue.text: Daniel for one, say, ever a money-grubber

indicators.note: say means the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Daniel is an Old Testament prophet
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A biblical seer, it seems, forever chasing money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes excessive gains, especially exploiting a shortage, is greedy for money.

clue.text: Boon companion, mostly of ashen appearance

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: pale means looking ashen

explanation.surface: A close friend looking rather wan.
explanation.definitionFit: A chum or mate is a close companion.

clue.text: Occurring again and again without beginning or end

explanation.surface: Something that repeats forever with no start or finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both perpetual, as in constant complaints, and having no start or finish in time.

clue.text: Student is sent out — joins the cause

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A pupil is expelled and goes off to sign up for a movement.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up, especially for military service, is to join a cause.
